payload.learning_objective: Realize that stacked ring-rectangles form a triangle with base 2πR and height R, whose area equals πR² — the circle area formula

mini_spec.title: Adding Ring Areas with Accumulator
mini_spec.manipulated_variable: A slider or draggable handle that controls how far through the radius the sweep has progressed (from 0 to R), adding ring areas one by one
mini_spec.primary_visual_feedback: As the student drags the slider outward, horizontal bars appear and stack upward, each bar's width proportional to 2πr for that ring's radius. The bars form a triangle shape. A running area counter displays the accumulated sum, approaching πR² as the sweep completes. The formula 2πr × dr is shown above the currently-adding ring.
mini_spec.goal_structure: Guided sweep from 0 to full radius R, with the payoff being the completed triangle and the area equaling πR²
mini_spec.causal_chain_exposed: Current sweep position r, the ring being added with its area formula 2πr × dr displayed, the running total of accumulated area, the triangle dimensions labeled (base = 2πR when complete, height = R), and the final area calculation ½ × 2πR × R = πR²
mini_spec.trace_strategy: All added bars remain visible, building up the triangle progressively; this accumulation IS the concept
mini_spec.aha_moment: The moment the sweep completes and the student sees that the stacked bars form a perfect triangle with base 2πR and height R — and that the triangle area formula gives exactly πR², revealing where the circle area formula comes from

payload.target_misconception: Students may not see why the stacked strips form exactly a triangle shape, or may not connect the triangle dimensions to the formula
payload.section_context: Final section and the aha moment. This is where everything comes together and the formula πR² emerges from the geometry.
payload.design_brief: This lesson derives the circle area formula πr² using concentric rings. This is the culminating section where the triangle shape is explicitly connected to the area formula. Show the triangle with labeled dimensions (base = 2πR, height = R) and the area calculation. The running total counter is key — it should show the accumulated area approaching πR² as the student sweeps through.
payload.proposition: When all ring-rectangles are lined up by radius, they form a triangle with base 2πR and height R, whose area is ½ × 2πR × R = πR²
payload.narrative_draft:
Here's the aha moment. The stacked rectangles form a triangle. Look at its dimensions: the base is the longest rectangle — the outer circumference, 2πR. The height is the full radius R.

Drag the slider to sweep from the center outward. Watch each ring's area (2πr × dr) add to the stack. The bars grow wider as r increases, forming that characteristic triangular profile. The running total shows your accumulated area climbing toward a familiar value.

When you reach the full radius, the triangle is complete. Its area? Half base times height: ½ × 2πR × R = πR². That's not a formula handed down from above — it's the inevitable consequence of how circles are built from rings.

contract.student_changes: drags a slider to sweep through the radii
contract.student_sees: bars stack upward forming a triangle; area counter shows the sum approaching πR²
